      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.VertexRepresentation.dense_kingEvaluationPoints {k R I J : Type u} [Field k] [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] (b : Module.Basis J k R) (d : I → ℕ) (e : I → R) (w : I → ℤ) :

      Each relevant prime omits a positive-degree form. Multiplying by this form detects every homogeneous component of an element on the evaluation locus.

      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.VertexRepresentation.subsingleton_closedPoints_iff_kingEvaluationPoints {k R I J : Type u} [Field k] [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] (b : Module.Basis J k R) (d : I → ℕ) (e : I → R) (w : I → ℤ) :
      {p : ProjectiveSpectrum (kingGrading b d e w) | IsClosed {p}}.Subsingleton ↔ (kingEvaluationPoints b d e w).Subsingleton

      Since evaluation points are closed and dense, at most one of them exists exactly when the scheme has at most one closed point.

      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.VertexRepresentation.not_subsingleton_closedPoints_of_ratio {k R I J : Type u} [Field k] [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] (b : Module.Basis J k R) (d : I → ℕ) (e : I → R) (w : I → ℤ) (x y : VertexRepresentation d e) {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (f g : KingPiece b d e w m) (hx : ↑↑g x ≠ 0) (hy : ↑↑g y ≠ 0) (hsep : ↑↑f x * ↑↑g y ≠ ↑↑f y * ↑↑g x) :
      ¬{p : ProjectiveSpectrum (kingGrading b d e w) | IsClosed {p}}.Subsingleton

      Two evaluations on the same chart give distinct closed points whenever the ratio of two forms of the same degree takes distinct values.
